Peru’s Electric Utilities Sector Reports Solid Growth Amid Steady Demand

Peru’s electric utilities sector posted stable growth in the first quarter of 2024, according to data released this week by the Peruvian Association of Electric Companies (APEE). The industry’s total electricity sales rose 4.2% year-on-year, driven by increased industrial activity and resilient residential demand.

ElectroAndes, one of the sector’s leading firms, reported quarterly revenues of PEN 1.15 billion, up from PEN 1.09 billion in Q1 2023. The company attributed the improvement to higher demand in Lima’s southern industrial corridor and ongoing grid expansion in the Arequipa region. "We are seeing sustained growth in both the manufacturing and mining sectors, which continue to be key drivers for electricity consumption," said Mariela Huamán, ElectroAndes’ Chief Financial Officer.

APEE’s data showed a 3.7% uptick in residential consumption, as population growth and new housing developments in urban centers bolstered usage. Meanwhile, commercial and small business segments registered a modest 2.8% increase. Generation from renewable sources continued to rise, accounting for 23% of total output, up from 20% a year earlier—reflecting ongoing investment in solar and wind projects across the south coast.

Analysts at Lima-based consultancy Energia21 noted that the sector’s outlook remains positive. "With steady regulatory support and robust infrastructure investments, Peru’s electric utilities are well positioned for continued expansion," said senior analyst Diego Lizárraga.

Industry observers expect further gains as new hydroelectric and solar plants come online later this year. No major disruptions have been reported, with operators highlighting grid stability and supply reliability throughout the quarter.
